evidence.excerpt: This paper reports a formulation development exercise carried out with a regional flexible-packaging converter. The target was to lower the required jaw temperature on a 300 bags/min VFFS line from 125 °C to below 110 °C without reducing seal strength below 25 N/25 mm or compromising hot-tack performance. Starting from a commercial 40 µm mLLDPE monolayer film, two modifications were evaluated: (i) partial substitution of the mLLDPE base resin with a 1-octene-based very-low-density polyethylene (VLDPE, density 0.900 g/cm³) at 10–25 wt%, and (ii) increasing seal-layer thickness from 40 to 50 µm in a three-layer coextrudate with OPP and tie. VLDPE addition at 20 wt% lowered SIT by 9 °C and enabled 26 N/25 mm plateau seal strength at 108 °C. Increasing film thickness to 50 µm without VLDPE gave a 5 °C SIT reduction. The combination of 20 wt% VLDPE and 50 µm gauge achieved a usable sealing window of 106–138 °C, a 32 °C range versus 18 °C for the commercial film. Line trials on a production VFFS machine confirmed seal integrity of filled pouches under 1.5 bar air pressure.
